what_this_is: PERCEPTUAL-FORMS-001F. The reference corpus for the perceptual-form benchmark: six real
works and four adversarial controls, each resolved to an institution and an accession
number where one exists, with its rights status recorded rather than assumed.
NO IMAGE BYTES ARE COMMITTED BY THIS LANE, for any entry, including the ones whose licence
would permit it. A manifest points at a lawful source and records what a fetched copy must
hash to; a checkout carries no painting. That keeps a public repository free of a rights
question nobody has to answer, and it keeps the corpus verifiable — `digest` is the promise,
and a copy that does not match it is a different picture.
TWO OF THE SIX NAMED WORKS ARE IN COPYRIGHT until the 2040s, and two more are public-domain
paintings whose only published reproductions are not freely licensed. Those four are
recorded as `reference_only`: identity resolved, rights stated, bytes not fetchable by this
lane. Where a freely licensed work of the same perceptual structure exists, it is named in
`open_access_alternate` — a stand-in for the measurement, never a substitute for the
identity. See RIGHTS.md for the full findings and the four unresolved questions.
THE ADVERSARIAL CONTROLS ARE ALREADY IN THE REPOSITORY. Lane C's model laboratory drew fog,
a tree behind a fence, a figure behind a table and a crowded plaza as synthetic images with
known alpha. They are referenced here by path and digest rather than redrawn, so the two
lanes cannot drift into testing different pictures.
retrieval_method: Institutional collection pages and public collection APIs, read on the retrieval date.
Every accession number below was read from the holding institution's own record or its
public API, not from an aggregator. Where no institution holds a work under the title the
build named, `identity.resolved` is false and `identity_notes` says what was found instead.

why_this_work: Deep architectural perspective with a receding courtyard: many nested extents (arcade,
bay, arch, doorway) whose containment is unambiguous to a person and whose boundaries
are long, straight and mostly unoccluded. It is the easiest honest test of
extent.hierarchy and topology.containment_tree — if a producer cannot build a tree here,
the failure is not the picture's fault.

identity.title: A Man kneels before a Woman in the Courtyard of a Renaissance Palace
identity.also_known_as: The Courtyard of a Renaissance Palace
identity.acquisition: Bequeathed by Lieutenant-Colonel J. H. Ollney, 1837
identity_notes: The build names the short title. The National Gallery's current catalogue title is the
longer one recorded above; both refer to NG141 and there is no ambiguity.
The figures are probably not by Steenwyck — he painted architecture and collaborated
on staffage. Irrelevant to the geometry, recorded so an attribution question later
does not read as a corpus error.

licence_notes: The National Gallery publishes low-resolution collection images under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0
and licenses high-resolution files commercially through its picture library. NC blocks
the commercial half of a research corpus and ND is a direct problem for a benchmark,
whose entire product is derivative: an annotation mask over an image is an adaptation.

open_access_alternate.title: A Renaissance Portico with Elegant Figures
open_access_alternate.caveat: a 11.1 cm tondo on copper, and the Met's published file is a black-and-white plate. Same painter, same architecture, and a poor substrate for boundary work — usable for hierarchy, not for edge quality

why_this_work: Flat, hard-edged, unmodelled forms with long cast shadows and an arcade receding to a
vanishing point: relations between things are stark and their SHADOWS are the reason
this slot exists. Asked where the tower is, a person may include or exclude the shadow
it throws — the competing-extent problem in its most legible form, and the reason the
matrix points topology.pair_relation here rather than at a busier picture.

open_access_alternate.title: unresolved
open_access_alternate.why: the perceptual property this slot tests — flat unmodelled masses with long detached cast shadows — is characteristic of a movement whose principal figures all died after 1955. No public-domain substitute was identified. The synthetic control `competing-extents` covers the same failure exactly and is what the matrix actually scores against.

why_this_work: A photograph, not a painting, and that is the point: the corpus needs one entry where
the geometry is real rather than depicted, so a producer cannot pass by learning what
paint looks like. Repeating bays, a scissor arch, and a nave arcade whose members touch
along long shared edges — the cleanest available test of adjacency at scale.

why_this_work: A Cubist interior is in the corpus because it breaks the assumption every other entry
shares: that an object has ONE extent. A guitar shown simultaneously from two angles has
two legitimate outlines and a person asked to segment it must choose an ontology before
they can draw. That is what extent.hypothesis_set and topology.uncertain_relation_set
exist for, and no naturalistic picture tests it honestly.

open_access_alternate.title: Still Life before an Open Window, Place Ravignan
open_access_alternate.institution: Philadelphia Museum of Art (Louise and Walter Arensberg Collection)
open_access_alternate.caveat: Gris is the one major Cubist whose work is out of copyright by age, and the perceptual structure is right — a tabletop, a window, a balcony, severe planar fragmentation. Two caveats travel with it: PD-Art rests on the doctrine that a faithful photograph of a two-dimensional public-domain work carries no new copyright, which is settled in the United States and contested in several EU states; and the Met's own records flag its Gris holdings `isPublicDomain: false` with no published image, so the Met is not a byte source for this artist even though the artist is out of copyright. See RIGHTS.md.

why_this_work: A painted architectural fantasy: perfectly regular, sharply lit, and constructed rather
than observed, so the boundaries are the crispest in the corpus. It is where boundary
ring reconstruction should be near-exact — which makes it the right place to catch a
producer that smooths, because here there is nothing to smooth away.

identity.title: Gallery of a Palace with Ornamental Architecture and Columns
identity.also_known_as: A Seven-Part Decorative Sequence: A Gallery
identity.acquisition: Purchased with the support of the Stichting tot Bevordering van de Belangen van het Rijksmuseum, 1958
identity_notes: THE BUILD'S TITLE DOES NOT RESOLVE. 'Perspective Fantasy of a Palace' appears on
print-reproduction and replica-selling sites and on no museum record found on the
retrieval date. Two candidates were considered and one chosen:
· The National Gallery NG1010, 'An Architectural Fantasy', 1634 — closest to the
build's title, and its reproductions are CC BY-NC-ND at low resolution only.
· Rijksmuseum SK-A-3937, recorded above — a palace gallery rather than a square, and
freely licensed at full resolution.
SK-A-3937 is the entry because a benchmark needs a picture it can lawfully use more
than it needs a title match. `resolved` is false to keep the discrepancy visible: this
is not the work the build named, and somebody should confirm the substitution.

why_this_work: A laid table: many small objects at a single scale, overlapping, on a plain ground. The
negative space between them is legible and bounded, which is what topology.negative_
space_field needs and what an architectural interior cannot provide — in a nave the
space between piers is the space you stand in and has no edge.

why_this_work: The required fog/veil/smoke control. An extent whose edge the picture does not contain:
a producer must return a graded field or refuse, and the failure to catch is a hard
mask returned with a confident boundary that nothing measured.

identity.title: soft-fog and hair-veil
identity_notes: Two images, and the pair is the test. `soft-fog` is genuine fractional occupancy and
`hair-veil` is fractional COVERAGE by sub-pixel filaments — the model is not unsure
where the hair is. A producer that reports its own doubt scores the same on both, and
that is the discrimination the pair exists to make.

access.digest_note: checked against Lane C's own manifest by `perception_lab_form_benchmark.py atlas`, so the two lanes cannot drift into testing different pictures

why_this_work: The required tree-behind-fence / river-behind-bridge control. One entity cut into five
by an occluder, so `extent.fragment_set` must find five pieces and refuse to say they
are one, and `extent.fused_hypothesis` must propose the grouping as a hypothesis with
grounds rather than as a measurement.

identity.title: fence-tree
identity_notes: Paired with `false-twins` in Lane C's corpus and with `false-similarity` here: one
scene where fragments ARE one entity and one where identical-looking fragments are
not. A producer that groups on appearance passes the first and fails the second, and
either alone is a test it can pass by having one bias.

access.digest_note: checked against Lane C's own manifest

why_this_work: The required person-behind-table control. The hidden pixels are known EXACTLY, because
the figure was drawn before the bar covered it — which makes this the only place an
amodal completion can be scored against a fact rather than against another opinion.

identity.title: occluder-table
identity_notes: The synthetic control has no `unknown` part: the figure is entirely within the frame,
so every pixel is either seen or hidden. This benchmark's own `partition` control adds
a figure that runs off the frame edge, because a partition with only two parts cannot
catch a producer that has nowhere to put what nothing settles.

access.digest_note: checked against Lane C's own manifest

why_this_work: The required crowd/plaza control. Sixty marks with a known east/west split: there is no
single object to outline, so a producer must answer with a density field and a count,
and the two can fail independently.

identity.title: crowd-plaza
identity_notes: Lane C pairs it with `windows-facade` (a regular grid) and `sparse-objects` (three
well-separated blobs). The three together separate 'can count' from 'can count when
the spacing is regular' from 'can count when there is nothing to count'.
